summary: Verified score 7.3/10. Not on par: the score is below 7.5. No blocker is open. Sensitivity PASS: re-checked portrait.png, splash.png and the match crops. The face plate carries a blue star slit and cheek lines, so it does not read as horror, a hockey mask or a blank mannequin. The crest is a low transverse bar. There is no hood, and the shape above the helm in the splash is the sword hilt. M1 (base splash) is CONFIRMED major. In splash.png the figure is small and off to the right, the raised forearm hides the helm, most of the blade leaves the frame, and the posterize finish turns the figure into flat blobs (flat-neighbour 0.35). M2 is DOWNGRADED to minor because its new evidence is a QA-tool artifact. art/tools/three_snapshot.mjs has no form handling. ervet.glb ships the three blades as separate nodes (form_base, form_great, form_great_1 accent seams, form_hilt), and the snapshot draws all of them on top of each other. So three_ervet.png and three_ervet_great.png are the same all-forms render (see _harness/_shots/closing_ervet_v_sheets.png), and the 'base blade already carries Great's seams' claim is false. In the match (closing_ervet_r2_close2.png, closing_ervet_r2_close_x3.png, closing_ervet_r2_gfx_game0_x4.png) the base blade is a plain pale bar with no blue zigzags. What remains is the first review's minor: the blade does not read as glass. Whether Great looks different in the match was not measured. m1 is CORRECTED but kept minor. idle_lobby is not frozen: ervet.py:2014-2039 keys a 16 deg blade twist (_grounded twist=16), 10-14 deg head turns and a knuckle tap. The reviewer's FK probe measured only the swing of the blade axis and says itself that twist was not measured. Hips are static (0.0 cm). m2-m5 confirmed. The score moves up 0.1 from the reviewer's 7.2 because one of the two majors falls away, but the base key art is still a visible miss at the loading screen. Frame timing was NOT MEASURED: load was 45-57 during this verify.

findings.title: Base splash hides the face and crops off the signature blade, and the posterize finish flattens the figure
findings.what: splash.png: the figure takes about a third of the card on the right. The raised forearm crosses the helm, so the star visor is buried. Most of the blade leaves the top of the frame. The posterize finish makes flat blobs (flat-neighbour 0.35), and the warm key turns the blue-grey model cream and tan.
findings.evidence: art/out/fighters/ervet/splash.png (viewed full frame); _harness/_shots/closing_ervet_r2_splash_head.png; _harness/_reports/closing_ervet_r2_card_luma.txt; art/blender/fighters/ervet.py:101-102 (cast_a3 t 0.25, 'the raised blade leaves the frame').
findings.gauge: A LoL base splash frames the face or helm and the signature weapon together as the focal pair, in painted form that matches the in-game palette.
findings.fix: Re-stage the base card from Ervet's own guard or Shatter wind-up with the blade fully in frame and the helm clear of both arms. Replace the posterize pass with a softer paint filter and painted rims. Use a cooler dawn key.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced on the shipped splash.png. Severity is right: the card is the first art the player sees at load and draft, and it fails the 'who is this' read. It is not a blocker (no sensitivity or function issue).

findings.title: The dawnglass blade reads as an opaque plank in the match
findings.what: In the match the base blade is a plain opaque pale bar with no glass value structure. The reviewer's main new claim, that the base blade already carries Great's zigzag seams, is false. It comes from art/tools/three_snapshot.mjs drawing every form node at once (form_base, form_great, form_great_1 seams, form_hilt), so the 'base' and 'great' QA sheets are the same overlaid render.
findings.evidence: _harness/_shots/closing_ervet_v_sheets.png (three_ervet.png over three_ervet_great.png: the same all-forms render, with seams and both blades overlaid); ervet.glb nodes 33-36 = form_base, form_great, form_great_1(accent), form_hilt; three_snapshot.mjs has no form option (grep 'form' finds nothing); in-game blade without zigzags: _harness/_shots/closing_ervet_r2_close2.png, closing_ervet_r2_gfx_game0_x4.png.
findings.gauge: LoL crystal or glass weapons read through painted value structure (bright bevels, a cooler core, one glint).
findings.fix: Paint a glass value read on the base blade: bright bevels, a cooler core, one diagonal glint. Separately, capture Great in the match (sim form great) before claiming it matches base. A form filter in three_snapshot would make the QA sheets truthful.
findings.verifierNote: Downgraded from major to minor, which is the first review's own severity for the glass read. The 'form difference absent' evidence is a tooling artifact.

findings.title: idle_lobby is subdued (no weight shift), not frozen
findings.what: The clip twists the grounded blade 16 deg, turns the head 10-14 deg and taps with a knuckle. The hips never move and there is no breath or weight shift, so the showcase idle reads as quiet.
findings.evidence: art/blender/fighters/ervet.py:2014-2039 (_grounded twist=16.0, head keys (-2,10,6)/(2,-10,-14), tap keys); _harness/_reports/closing_ervet_r2_fk.txt hips 0.0 cm, and twist not measured.
findings.gauge: A LoL showcase idle sells one clear beat with visible weight shift.
findings.fix: Raise the twist to 35-45 deg so the flat flashes, and add a 2-3 cm hip shift and a chest breath.
findings.verifierNote: Kept minor. The wording 'frozen' and 'beat does not exist' is wrong: the twist beat exists but is small.
